coupling: The first edit removes the serializer buffer's fixed 64-byte growth allowance while still requesting the exact required capacity. The second edit reserves one full 64-byte block for short writes and rounds longer raw-byte reservations down to a 64-byte boundary. Either edit alone is safe: exact reservations still allocate enough memory, and the original 64-byte allowance covers the removed partial block. Together, a 257-byte payload reserves only 256 bytes after the already-written 256-byte prefix, then copies 257 bytes into the malloc-backed serializer buffer, producing an ASan heap-buffer-overflow.
